Faculty Senate Executive Committee Report #2024-2025-3 January 23, 2025 Faculty Senate Meeting Context (from JCODL 2022-2023 final report): “Several years ago (circa 2013), URI adopted definitions of online and blended learning (Face to face [< 25% online], Blended [25-75% online], and Online [75-100% online]), with the implicit, but unstated, assumption that the online portion was asynchronous.
The COVID era of remote instruction gave rise to additional approaches to remote instruction and the need to reflect all available modality options and to provide clear, comprehensible and accessible definitions and descriptions for the benefit of faculty and students.” Rationale: Definitions for Course Methods of Instruction are not currently memorialized in the University Manual and the current need to update related descriptions provides an opportunity to ensconce standardized language in the University Manual, where it will be easily found and understood.
The language is proposed for insertion into Chapter 8, Academic Regulations (Regulations for Students), Section 30, Courses.

Making JCODL’s suggested changes requires removing ‘Online’ from the approved ‘Methods of Instruction’ and removing the term “in class” from the descriptions of ‘Laboratory’ and ‘Studio’.
Because over 770 current ‘online’-method courses will need to be assigned to one of the other methods, faculty/departments will be allowed to update the method of current ‘online’ courses directly with the registrar without going through the standard course modification process.
Due to the volume of required changes, the new methods will take effect starting in the Fall 2026 semester.
Existing Language: - The Four Hundred Fifty-First Report of the Curricular Affairs Committee - https://web.uri.edu/facsen-old/curricular-matters/method-of-instruction/ “ Lecture: A course in which the primary method is presentation and students are expected to participate in a variety of ways, such as small-group discussions, questions and answers, writing-exercises, etc.
Laboratory: In-class applied course work, generally involving experimentation or observation, typically using special equipment (including computers and specialized software).

Recitation: Separate sections of a lecture course regularly scheduled for discussion.
Studio: In-class, supervised work with an emphasis on performance and creativity in which faculty instruct, assist, and critique.
Seminar: Course offered to a small group (usually no more than 20 students) where participants actively exchange ideas and findings based on readings or research.

Independent Study: One-on-one instruction in which the student enters into an agreement with the instructor that defines the focus of inquiry and nature of activities.
Includes tutorials, directed readings, special projects.
Practicum: Structured experiences where the primary aim is to connect theory with practice.
Includes clinics, internships, externships, student teaching, field experiences.
May include regular class meetings.
Workshop: Similar to a seminar, with emphasis on applied rather than theoretical learning, but not offered for degree-program credit.
Online: A course that is delivered entirely online. GC: Grand Challenge
GRAND CHALLENGE
At the center of Grand Challenge courses is a complex issue of contemporary significance, and in those courses students will be given the opportunity to explore, question, and wrestle with the issue. The contemporary challenge should be evident to both the students and reviewers in the title of the course, the syllabus, and assignments.
* Explain how the course title, syllabus, and assignments demonstrate the contemporary challenge addressed by the course.
INTERDISCIPLINARY
Interdisciplinary study draws on multiple disciplinary perspectives and integrates their insights to produce a comprehensive understanding. It is a process of answering questions, solving problems, or addressing topics that are too broad or complex to be dealt with adequately by a single discipline.

When reviewing the syllabus, students and the Curriculum Committee must be able to recognize the contributions of at least two disciplinary perspectives and how students will make interdisciplinary connections in the assignments, activities, and/or experiences.
* Explain how the course incorporates at least two disciplinary perspectives and provides opportunities for students to make interdisciplinary connections through assignments, activities, and/or experiences.
* Provide an abbreviated reading list organized by discipline that demonstrates the course’s disciplinary perspectives, and explain how each disciplinary perspective is integrated into major course assignments and activities
ETHICS
Each Grand Challenge course presents the ethical challenges associated with the issue and provides students with the skills to recognize such challenges as well as apply ethical concepts/frameworks in considering the ramifications of alternative actions.
* Identify the ethical framework students will use to weigh and evaluate issues. Indicate where this framework is addressed in the course schedule.
* Provide a list of readings that address the ethical dimensions of the course topic.
* Explain how ethics is incorporated into some or all of the course assignments and activities.
